subject: EOQ load test — temporary rate band relief request
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Finlytics DevOps <devops@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary rate band relief for EOQ load test

Hi Jonas,

We're running a coordinated end-of-quarter load test next Wednesday (May 23) as part of our production readiness push for a new feature roll-out. Traffic profile: short 4-hour spike with ~1.2M tokens/min sustained on the Generate endpoint and ~12k requests/min, predominantly single-turn inference.

We're asking Redwood for a short-term relaxation of the rate band (throttling/fairness) so our test doesn't get prematurely throttled by fair-share enforcement. Specifically: a 4-hour window, east-us region, allow higher per-route concurrency and a higher burst cap for our API key. We'll instrument traces and share logs. Attachment: EOQ-load-test-plan.pdf (high level schedule and expected traffic).

Could you confirm what information you need to evaluate and what the approval process looks like? We want to avoid disrupting other customers — happy to work with you on guardrails.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform Reliability, Finlytics
elena.park@finlytics.com
+1 415-555-0192

--
Attachment: EOQ-load-test-plan.pdf (3 pages, load profile + rollback plan)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate band relief for EOQ load test

Thanks Elena — appreciate the heads-up and for sharing the plan. Quick notes and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the exception safely: 

- Proposed window: you said May 23, 4 hours. Please confirm start/end times (UTC).
- Traffic shape: 1.2M tokens/min and ~12k req/min — is that peak or sustained for the whole 4 hours?
- Which API key(s) / routes will be used (e.g., /v1/generate, /v1/chat)?

Operational approach we're proposing:
- Temporary rate-band relief scoped to your API key + east-us region only.
- Hard token cap at X tokens/min (we'll set this in the emergency guardrail) and an absolute global safety cutoff if infrastructure effects are detected.
- Instrumentation: please enable X-Request-ID and include trace headers. We'll monitor in real time and can throttle earlier if we see cross-customer impact.

I've looped in Marissa (SRE lead for capacity operations) and Ben (account lead) — Marissa will validate the capacity plan and confirm whether we can provide a per-route burst uplift for that 4-hour window. Ben, do you want to propose commercial/credits terms for burns outside the committed baseline?

If you can answer the questions above and drop the exact start/end in UTC, I can escalate to ops and get an approval decision within one business day.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

> On Thu, May 16, 2028 at 08:12 AM Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com> wrote:
> > We're running a coordinated end-of-quarter load test next Wednesday (May 23)...

From: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Finlytics DevOps <devops@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate band relief for EOQ load test

Thanks, Jonas — quick answers below: 

- Window: May 23, 14:00 UTC — May 23, 18:00 UTC (4 hours).
- Traffic: the 1.2M tokens/min is the expected sustained peak for the first 45 minutes as we ramp; then we expect 600k tokens/min for the remaining window.
- Routes/API keys: primary route is /v1/generate using key fk-prod-41; secondary is a small number of calls to /v1/embeddings (not part of the high-volume path).

We'll enable X-Request-ID and tracing for the test. Attaching the more detailed test plan and a small instrumentation checklist you can share with Marissa: redwood-instrumentation-checklist.md.

We'd like the temporary uplift to be scoped exactly to fk-prod-41 and to the east-us region. We understand and accept a global safety cutoff; we'll stop the test immediately if you alert us.

Are there any commercial implications for a short-term uplift like this (credits or overage bill)? Ben, would appreciate your guidance.

—Elena

--
Attachment: redwood-instrumentation-checklist.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate band relief for EOQ load test

Elena — thanks for the details and the checklist. We've reviewed the plan and can provision a scoped, temporary relaxation with the following constraints: 

- Approved window: 2028-05-23 14:00 UTC -> 2028-05-23 18:00 UTC, east-us only.
- Scope: API key fk-prod-41 only, routes /v1/generate (primary) and /v1/embeddings (secondary limited to 10% of throughput).
- Uplift: increase per-route burst cap to 1.5x baseline and raise soft concurrency limit to allow the requested token rate. We will configure an enforced hard token ceiling at 1.4M tokens/min for that key.
- Safety: global emergency cutoff will remain active. If cross-customer impacts are detected we will terminate the window immediately and send an incident update.
- SLA: this is a temporary operational exception for rate-band enforcement only — it does not change SLA uptime or latency commitments beyond the standard contract.

Operational asks for Finlytics before we enable the window:
- Confirm the test start/end (reply with exact times — already provided above, confirming acceptable).
- Confirm you'll send traces with X-Request-ID and that your team will accept real-time monitoring pings.
- Provide a single point-of-contact pager/phone for the window.

Commercial: Ben, suggested handling is a one-off consumption credit against the Q2 overage bucket; suggest we draft a short amendment to the order. Ben — can you prepare a one-line amendment and confirm?

Once Elena confirms the three operational asks, I'll schedule capacity ops to enable the temporary config and share the monitoring dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.internal/monitoring/FT-2028-Q2-EXP01

Marissa Cole
SRE, Capacity Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
